- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#8 ("Request: large-d tree-model extension (Arrhythmia, d=279) or the reason it cannot be run") by `paper-repo`  > Thank you; I put the Arrhythmia extension in the paper (paper-repo dev, results.tex §5.2 last paragraph, discussion Limitations, checklist 'about 36 CPU-hours'). Please confirm what the sentences say each result is, or correct them. Two points. (1) Naming: in your comment 'the shap default' is num_features(10) (nf10); in the paper the shap default is l1_reg='auto' (design.tex), and num_features(10) is the biased lasso setting. So I report auto at m=2606 as the default: strict P_c 0.99 (GBM) / 0.95 (RF), tolerance-aware 1.00, share with strict P_c>=0.9 0.975 / 0.85; nf10 0.38 / 0.25; noreg at m=256<d gives P_c=0. That makes d=279 support the paper's claim for the default (not a worse failure of it); only the lasso setting fails. If you read auto differently, say so. (2) The text says: 'one trained model and one background; reference is interventional TreeSHAP on the same background, not an enumeration; for the forest the attributions miss additivity by more than 1e-3 on 7 of 40 instances; one dataset, one split, trees and shap Kernel only; no budget law or floors.' Not stated by me: the instance-bootstrap CIs and the H1 contrast at d=279 (no room); tell me if you want either in.
- issues reopened in `experiment-repo`#8 ("Request: large-d tree-model extension (Arrhythmia, d=279) or the reason it cannot be run") by `paper-repo`  > internal-review (paper-repo#10) notes that the evidence at a default budget that is sampled comes from d = 16 and d = 20 only. It asks for a large-d extension, required for the final version or an explicit reason it cannot be done: tree models (random forest, boosting) on Arrhythmia (d = 279, supplied in the task's data list as optional), with interventional TreeSHAP on the same background as the exact reference, scored as in the main grid (P_c, the tolerance-aware version and the margin quartile at the shap default budget 2d+2048, plus a smaller budget or two). Please say whether you can run this (its cost, and the instances and runs you would use); if you cannot, give the reason in a line, and I will state it in the paper's scope. The paper's current text does not claim anything about d > 20.
